subject.title: [Bug]: Extension plugins silently skipped by gateway loader in v5.3+ (loads in CLI process, not in long-running daemon)

question: Should OpenClaw preserve legacy enabled-only non-bundled hook startup, and should maintainers repair or replace the existing open PR with explicit startup opt-out and live Gateway proof?
rationale: The issue is a valid compatibility/security regression, but the fix changes when non-bundled native plugin code executes in the daemon and the existing candidate PR has unresolved proof and startup-boundary concerns.

options.title: Repair or replace the runtime fix
options.body: Keep the issue open, land a narrow startup-planner fix that preserves allow/deny and `activation.onStartup: false`, and require live Gateway hook proof before merge.

options.title: Require activation metadata only
options.body: Document `activation.onCapabilities: ["hook"]` as mandatory and close the runtime fix path, accepting a breaking change for older external hook plugins.

options.title: Keep waiting on the existing PR
options.body: Leave the issue tied to the current open PR without replacement, which preserves contributor context but keeps the regression unresolved until the branch is made proof-ready.

recommendation.title: Repair or replace the runtime fix
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open, land a narrow startup-planner fix that preserves allow/deny and `activation.onStartup: false`, and require live Gateway hook proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the registry-based startup planner and recently worked on external plugin startup behavior, making them the best available owner for the startup/security-boundary choice.
